07.10 Seattle

What is the Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic?

The Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic (STP) is a 206-mile supported ride from the University of Washington in Seattle to Holladay Park in Portland, Oregon, held the second weekend of July. Riders finish in one day or two, with the two-day overnight at Centralia College. Cascade Bicycle Club has run it since 1979, and 6,400 riders took part in 2026. The next edition is July 10–11, 2027.

How the Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic started

Cascade Bicycle Club started the STP in 1979. That first year it was a race, and Jerry Baker of Seattle won it. In 1981 the club changed the format to a recreational ride open to any speed and ability, which is what it has been since.

The ride grew fast. Cascade reports a record 10,000 participants in 1991, and for years the club capped the field at 10,000 and sold out in spring. In 2018, according to Wikipedia, 1,854 of nearly 8,000 riders attempted the full distance in one day.

The 2020 and 2021 rides were cancelled because of COVID-19. The event came back in 2022. The 2026 edition, presented by Alaska Airlines, had 6,400 riders and sold out. The 2027 ride will be the 48th.

What to expect on the day

The start is the E-18 parking lot at the University of Washington. One-day riders leave between 5:00 and 5:30 a.m.; two-day riders leave between 5:30 and 7:30 a.m. Cascade tells riders not to leave after 7:30 a.m., because the luggage trucks close and you will be behind the support services.

The route is 206 miles with about 5,100 feet of climbing on country roads that stay off I-5. Full rest stops are at mile 20 (IKEA in Renton), mile 55 (Spanaway Middle School), mile 109 (Chehalis Recreation Park), mile 147 (Riverside Park in Lexington) and mile 177 (St. Helens Elementary), with 13 smaller mini-stops in between. The official midpoint at mile 101 is Centralia College, which has medical, mechanical and food for purchase, plus overnight options for two-day riders.

The finish is Holladay Park near Lloyd Center in Portland. Portland Bicycling Club runs the finish line with up to 130 volunteers and also runs Friday buses to Seattle for Portland-based riders. Registration includes free snacks and drinks at the official stops.

Weather in Seattle for the Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic

Seattle in July is the driest month of the year: average high about 77°F, average low about 58°F, with only about 0.7 inches of rain and roughly 3.6 days with measurable precipitation. Expect a cool, damp 5 a.m. start and a warm afternoon south of Centralia.

The town guide

Ride, sleep, eat, fix the bike.

Seattle is a city you ride out of on trails and ferries. The Burke-Gilman runs from Shilshole Bay past the University of Washington to Bothell, almost all of it off the road. The Lake Washington loop is 50 miles around the lake. The Bainbridge ferry leaves Colman Dock downtown, and the Chilly Hilly course starts at the other end. Cascade Bicycle Club leads free group rides most days of the week, and its Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic leaves the University of Washington on July 10, 2027. Delta, Southwest and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026). Link light rail takes you and the bike from the airport to downtown in 38 minutes.

Fly into Seattle-Tacoma International (SEA), about 14 miles south of downtown. Link light rail leaves from the airport garage: trains every 8 to 10 minutes most of the day, 38 minutes to downtown, and on to the University of Washington; bikes roll on free. You don’t need a car. The Burke-Gilman, the West Seattle loop and the Bainbridge ferry start in the city, the north-lake loop can start at UW Station, and the lake loop passes Seward Park. Only Zoo Hill and the Carnation gravel loop want a car or a long ride out. Coming home from Portland after the STP, Amtrak Cascades has ten $5 bike racks on every train (Oct 2026), or Cascade’s own buses bring riders and bikes back to UW. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the ferry fare, each transit agency’s bike rules and the shops that rent.

Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic FAQ

Do I have to ride it in one day?

No. Most riders take two days and overnight in Centralia at mile 101. One-day riders start earlier, between 5:00 and 5:30 a.m.

How much climbing is there?

Cascade lists 5,100 feet of elevation gain over the 206 miles. The terrain is rolling with a few real hills, not mountainous.

Where does it start and finish?

It starts at the University of Washington E-18 lot on Walla Walla Road NE in Seattle and finishes at Holladay Park in Portland, Oregon.

Does it sell out?

Yes. The 2026 ride sold out ahead of its July 5 registration deadline. Member registration for 2027 is expected to re-open in January 2027.

What does registration include?

Free snacks and drinks at the official rest stops, luggage transport for two-day riders, a marked route and mechanical and medical support at the major stops.

How do I get back to Seattle?

Cascade sells return transportation and Portland Bicycling Club runs Friday buses from Portland to the start. Check the transportation details page on cascade.org when registration opens.
